questions: Does the operation cost i based on the original positions (1-indexed) of the elements being swapped, or based on the current positions of those elements in the permutation at the moment of the swap?
Is the goal to sort P into strictly increasing order (1,2,...,N), or could it be any sorted order (e.g., non-decreasing) given the permutation contains each number exactly once?
Are we allowed to perform swaps in any order, and is the total cost simply the sum of costs of each swap performed, regardless of sequence?
Should we find the minimum possible total cost to sort P, or any sequence of swaps that sorts it (since cost depends on chosen i)?
If multiple swap sequences achieve sorted order, do we need to output the minimum total cost among them?
Does the cost i refer to the index in the 1-based array at the time of the swap, or the value of the element at position i before swapping?
Is the operation allowed only on adjacent elements, and does 'swap P_i and P_{i+1}' mean swap the values at those positions?
Can we choose the same i multiple times in different operations, and does the cost remain i each time?
